newsitem.title: USA: U.S. university offers sextuplets free tuition.
newsitem.headline: U.S. university offers sextuplets free tuition.

text.p: The parents of sextuplets born last month in a New York City suburb had one less expense to worry about -- college tuition -- on Tuesday after the State University of New York at Stony Brook offered free tuition to all six, who would graduate in the class of 2015.
The offer, four years of school for six students, is worth $81,600 today, university officials told a news conference.

"Now I don't have to get that third or fourth job," joked the babies' father, Rocco Boniello, 30, a technician for the Nynex telephone company. Beverly Boniello, their mother, works as a mail carrier for the U.S. Postal Service.

The four girls and two boys were born at the university's hospital in Stony Brook, a New York City suburb, on March 24. The six -- Olivia Frederica, Sabrina Juliette, Sophia Betty, Stella Raquel, Trifon Robert and Gerard Martin -- remain in hospital incubators where they are doing "great," their parents said.
Beverly Boniello, 27, described the tuition offer as "an amazing, wonderful gift" and added, "This is just like the cherry on the sundae."
University president Shirley Strum Kenny said the tuition money will come from private endowment funds. She also gave the Boniellos six tiny Stony Brook T-shirts.
"We think of them as Stony Brook kids to begin, and we will think of them as Stony Brook kids coming up," she said.
The couple has been married 5-1/2 years. They have been getting donations and gifts as well as offers from media outlets around the world to buy their story, their attorney Kevin Mescall said.
